I will still start from what worked for me before, then make small changes where I think the money can come back in yield. On my 5 mu, I do not spread myself too thin, because every bag of fertilizer and every spray costs cash, and there are only 2 of us at home. I have well water, so I will use that advantage on cabbage, chili, and spinach, because these crops lose money fast if they stay dry. For fertilizer, I will not go light. Vegetables need feeding, especially cabbage and chili, and I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the harvest come down. For maize and kidney bean, I will keep the rate steadier, because those are easier to over-spend on. I also watch what nearby farmers do. If an improved or hybrid seed gave good stands and better picking last year, I will use it again. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage on the vegetable land because it is quicker and suits my small area, but I will plough the maize patch once to loosen the ground better. I will keep sprays to the crops that really need them, and I will not spray blindly if pressure is low, but I will not wait too long either if worms, aphids, or disease start to show.
